dataset.name: Topography, surface water distribution and subsurface structure in 2023 across an Arctic coastal tundra site near Utqiagvik, Alaska
description: Subsurface electrical resistivity tomography (ERT), active layer thickness measurements, photogrammetry, and topographic data were collected in September 2023 along a 475 m long, 20 m wide corridor that traverses various polygon types within the Barrow Environmental Observatory (BEO) on the Alaskan Arctic Coastal Plain, approximately 4 miles from the Beaufort Sea near Utqiaġvik, Alaska. These measurements were designed to assess decadal changes in surface water distribution, topography, and subsurface structure across this dynamic landscape. This archive contains the datasets acquired in 2023 and references to the datasets acquired previously at the same location. The ERT survey was conducted along the 475 m transect using 0.5 m electrode spacing and a roll-along acquisition strategy. Thaw layer thicknesses were measured with a tile probe along the same transect. Photogrammetry data were acquired using an unoccupied aerial vehicle (UAV) and were used to generate a digital elevation model and an RGB mosaic. A real-time kinematic (RTK) GPS was used to survey the ERT electrodes and the ground control points for the aerial imagery. The dataset contains 5 *.csv data files, 6 *.csv metadata files, and 6 *.tif files.

The Next-Generation Ecosystem Experiments: Arctic (NGEE Arctic), was a research effort to reduce uncertainty in Earth System Models by developing a predictive understanding of carbon-rich Arctic ecosystems and feedbacks to climate. NGEE Arctic was supported by the Department of Energy's Office of Biological and Environmental Research. The NGEE Arctic project had two field research sites: 1) located within the Arctic polygonal tundra coastal region on the Barrow Environmental Observatory (BEO) and the North Slope near Utqiagvik (Barrow), Alaska and 2) multiple areas on the discontinuous permafrost region of the Seward Peninsula north of Nome, Alaska. Through observations, experiments, and synthesis with existing datasets, NGEE Arctic provided an enhanced knowledge base for multi-scale modeling and contributed to improved process representation at global pan-Arctic scales within the Department of Energy's Earth system Model (the Energy Exascale Earth System Model, or E3SM), and specifically within the E3SM Land Model component (ELM).

measurementTechnique:
The ERT data acquisition geometry and inversion are described in the associated manuscript. Measured resistance values for 2023 are provided in three files, all with the same format. In the file ERTda_2023, several filters were applied. Measurements with absolute potential differences below 5 mV were removed. Apparent resistivity values below 2 Ω·m or above 2500 Ω·m, based on histogram analysis, were excluded. Configurations where the “n” (multiplier of AB distance to get BM) exceeded 5 were also removed. In addition, data showing more than 50% difference between reciprocal and normal readings were excluded, although reciprocal measurements were only available for a small subset of the dataset. Duplicate and reciprocal entries were also removed. Finally, for the 2011 survey, electrodes at 101 m and then every 84 m thereafter were removed due to a faulty connector in the cable.
The file ERTda_2023_similar.csv contains a further trimmed version of the 2023 dataset, including only measurements that are also present in the 2011 survey. The file ERTda_2023_sm_similar.csv is further reduced by excluding all configurations with “n” values greater than 4. This exclusion reduces the influence of data collected at greater depths and minimizes noise associated with the instrument’s multi-channel acquisition. The inverted resistivity values were computed using the dataset in ERTda_2023_similar.csv.
Thaw layer thickness measurements are provided for various dates. Additional data collected at the same locations can be obtained from the other datasets referenced in this archive.
The UAV data acquisition process is described in the associated manuscript. The RGB mosaic and digital elevation model (DEM) were reconstructed using Agisoft Metashape. Ground control points (GCPs) consisted of 20.3 cm square white targets placed approximately every 20 m along the right, middle, and left sides of the survey corridor, and were surveyed using RTK GPS. The DEM and RGB mosaic are provided in GeoTIFF format using NAD83 (2011), the 2012 geoid, and UTM Zone 4 North coordinates. Pixel resolution is approximately 5 cm. The zone within the GCP-controlled corridor is expected to have high spatial accuracy (better than 10 cm), whereas areas outside the corridor likely have much lower accuracy. The archive includes the original RGB mosaic and DEM covering the entire area in UTM coordinates (X_0_UTM), the extracted corridor projected into a local coordinate system (X_corridor_local), and the reprojected version of this local subset back into UTM coordinates (X_corridor_back2UTM).
